text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The national assembly said it will not grant the opposition official recognition because their representation in the 158-member parliament is below 50.

- Some top officials in former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP) are plotting to unseat him following the passing of new laws that ban him from contesting future presidential elections.
- Lawyers in all government departments, including those under the director of public prosecutions, went on strike on Tuesday to push for increased pay.
- Interest rates may go down in 1997 as a result of a budget surplus recorded last year, finance minister Ronald Penza said.
- The international media watchdog group, Reporters Sans Frontiers, has urged the government to drop plans to set up a council to regulate the media.
